newsitem.title: UK: UK's Norwich Union gives no clues on valuation.
newsitem.headline: UK's Norwich Union gives no clues on valuation.

text.p: UK mutual life and general insurer Norwich Union on Wednesday gave financial analysts little new information as to its likely value, following its earlier announcement that it is to float on the stock market.
"The valuation depends on the valuations of the businesses being transferred to the shareholders on which we've got very incomplete information," one insurance analyst told Reuters.

Norwich Union was initially concentrating on explaining its decision to go public to its policyholders, some 2.9 million of whom can each expect to receive shares worth between 500 and 1,000 stg, analysts said.

The valuation figure of 4.0 to 4.5 billion stg, which has been widely quoted in the press since Norwich Union announced it was considering demutualisation a year ago, was probably about right, analysts said.
"It doesn't look unreasonable to me," said Lehman Brothers insurance analyst Rob Procter.
Another noted that it was unusual for valuations to exceed a company's annual premium income, which for Norwich Union amounted to 4.7 billion stg in 1995.

Based on the information currently available, Norwich Union policyholders look set to receive around 2.0 billion stg, with some 2.5 billion stg of new money being raised from issue of shares on flotation, analysts said.

The changes necessary to bring one of the biggest UK insurers to market will take at least until summer 1997, but analysts said they did not expect the project to be derailed by a hostile takeover bid.
They pointed out that a hostile bid would have to secure the backing of policyholders and would probably have to be of the order of 5.0 billion stg, a price tag beyond the reach of most.
